payments.thereArePaymentsButNoneAre: There are payments here, but none of them are {0}.
payments.oneMovementOfMoney: One movement of money, and what is known about where it got to.
payments.inTheProvidersOwnWords: In the provider's own words. A decline for insufficient funds and a bank blocking the merchant need two different things done about them.
payments.noneOnlySettledPaymentsHave: None — only a settled payment has one
payments.raisedForAnInvoiceNotAClaim: Raised for an invoice, which is not a claim about what it settled — the ledger decides that, and a payment raised for one invoice can end up applied against another.
payments.receiptCouldNotBeExported: The receipt could not be exported
payments.whatHasMovedBetweenUs: Every movement between this account and the platform, newest first, with what the balance stood at after each one.
payments.accountCouldNotBeRead: The account could not be read
payments.noMoneyHasMovedYet: No money has moved between this account and the platform yet — nothing paid, nothing applied, nothing refunded.
payments.everyMovementAppearsHere: Every movement appears here as it happens. Nothing is ever edited or removed, so an empty statement means nothing has moved.
payments.runningBalanceOnlyOnTheFirstPag: The running balance is shown on the first page only. It is worked backwards from the account's closing figure, which a later page has no way to reach.
payments.statusHint.pending: Requested, and not yet money. A direct debit takes several working days and can still be refused after it has been accepted, so nothing here has arrived and there is no receipt to issue. Nothing to do but wait.
payments.statusHint.settled: The money arrived. This is the only state with a receipt, because a receipt is evidence that it did.
payments.statusHint.failed: The money never arrived — the card was declined, or the debit was refused. The reason the provider gave is shown beside it, and it decides what to do next: a fixable decline is a retry, a blocked merchant is a call to the bank.
payments.statusHint.returned: The money arrived and then left again: a direct debit pulled back inside its eight-week indemnity window, or a card charge disputed. It keeps its receipt number, because the receipt was genuinely issued at the time — this is a reversal of a payment that happened, not a payment that failed.
payments.thisRowIsDatedBy: This row is dated by when it was {0}.
payments.kindHint.card: Charged on the due date, or whenever an invoice is collected. Cards expire, and a collection that fails on an expired card is the avoidable kind.
payments.kindHint.directDebit: A mandate you signed at your bank. Collections take several working days to clear and can be recalled by you for eight weeks afterwards.
payments.kindHint.bankTransfer: Money you send yourself, quoting the invoice number. Nothing is stored here to charge, so nothing about it appears on this list.
payments.receiptOnlyWhenSettled: A receipt is evidence that money arrived, so there is one only for a settled payment. A payment still clearing has not arrived yet, and a reversed one keeps the number of the receipt it was issued at the time — but the money has since gone back.
payments.refusal.noMethodTitle: Nothing on file to pay with
payments.refusal.noMethodHint: There is no card or mandate on file to collect against. Adding one takes you to the payment provider's own page.
payments.refusal.settledHint: This invoice has nothing outstanding — it has been paid, credited, or both, since this screen was loaded. Nothing was collected.
payments.refusal.currencyHint: The money and the document are in different currencies, and nothing on the collection side converts between them. Which rate, on which day, and who absorbs the difference are commercial questions rather than ones a console should answer quietly.
payments.refusal.balanceHint: There is less on the account than was asked for. Applying more than is there would put the customer into arrears by bookkeeping rather than by anything they did or did not pay.
payments.expiringSoon: This card expires soon. Replacing it before then is the difference between a collection that works and one that fails on the due date — and only you can do it, at the provider.
payments.expired: This card has expired. A collection against it will fail. Add a replacement, which takes you to the provider's own page.
payments.nothingOnFileDetail: No card or mandate has been added, so invoices cannot be collected automatically and will have to be paid by transfer. Adding one takes you to our payment provider's own page — nothing you type there passes through this platform.
payments.addingAtTheProvider: This takes you to our payment provider's own page to enter the details. Nothing you type there reaches this platform — what comes back is a reference and a label like the ones above.
payments.removingAtTheProvider: Cards and mandates are removed at the provider rather than here, and the default is chosen there too. This platform holds only a reference to what you have on file, so it has nothing to delete.
payments.sessionUrlsMustBeHttps: This console is not being served over https, so there is no secure address to send you back to — and the provider only accepts one, because you arrive back having just typed a card number. Nothing was sent. Running the console locally? Start it with npm run dev:https. Otherwise this is one for whoever runs the installation.
payments.reasonHint.receipt: Money arrived and went onto the account. It is not yet against any particular invoice — that is a separate movement.
payments.reasonHint.allocation: Cash on the account was applied to an invoice, reducing what that invoice has outstanding.
payments.reasonHint.refund: Money was handed back off the account. The description is the reason somebody gave at the time, and it is the only record of why.
payments.reasonHint.return: A payment that had arrived was taken back — a direct debit recalled, or a card charge disputed. The money left the account again.
payments.reasonHint.creditNote: A credit note reduced what was owed. No money moved: the supplier agreed it was never owed in the first place.
payments.unappliedCashExplained: In credit: money has been paid that nothing has been applied to yet. Usually an overpayment, or a transfer that arrived before the invoice it was meant for. It is not lost — it is applied to the next invoice it fits, and it can be refunded instead.
payments.owedExplained: Owed: there is more on invoices than has been paid against them. The invoice list shows which ones, and what is still outstanding on each.
payments.squareExplained: Square. Everything paid has been applied, and nothing is outstanding.
payments.nothingHasMoved: Nothing has moved on this account yet — no payments, no allocations, nothing refunded. Not the same as being square, which is what a zero balance with entries behind it means.
payments.balancesNeverNet: Balances are held per currency and are never added together. A customer in credit in euro and in arrears in sterling owes sterling — combining the two would need a conversion rate, and nothing on this side of the platform converts anything.
payments.ledgerIsAppendOnly: The ledger is append-only. Nothing here is edited or removed, and a movement made in error is corrected by a further movement that says so — which is why every line has a description written at the time.
reconciliation.whatArrivedWithoutADocume: Money that arrived without a document to attach it to, and invoices that are late and how far they have been chased.
reconciliation.unappliedCouldNotBeRead: Unapplied cash could not be read
reconciliation.everyPaymentHasBeenApplie: Every payment that has arrived has been applied to something. Money that cannot yet be attributed shows up here rather than being guessed onto an invoice.
reconciliation.whatArrivedAndWhatItMight: What arrived on this account, and the open invoices it could belong to.
reconciliation.noPaymentsOnThisAccount: No payments have been recorded against this account.
reconciliation.nothingOpenToApplyItTo: Nothing open in this currency to apply it to. Nothing on the collection side converts, so money in one currency cannot be applied to a document in another — it stays on the account until an invoice in the same currency is raised, or it is refunded.
reconciliation.theLedgerNowShowsIt: The ledger now shows it against that invoice, and the invoice's outstanding figure has come down.
reconciliation.cashCouldNotBeApplied: The cash could not be applied
reconciliation.contextCouldNotBeRead: This account's payments and invoices could not be read
reconciliation.inTheBalancesOwnCurrency: In the balance's own currency. Nothing here converts, so a refund is always raised in the currency the money is sitting in.
reconciliation.refundCouldNotBeRecorded: The refund could not be recorded
reconciliation.moneyThatArrivedInTheBank: Money that arrived in the bank account, written down by whoever found it on the statement. It is settled the moment it is recorded, because it has already arrived.
reconciliation.theDayItLandedNotToday: The day the money landed on the statement, not the day you are recording it. Everything downstream is aged from this.
reconciliation.cannotBeInTheFuture: Money cannot have arrived in the future.
reconciliation.whateverThePayerWroteOnIt: Whatever the payer wrote on the transfer, kept exactly as typed. Frequently the only evidence of what it was for — and a reference that matches nothing still has to be readable by whoever works it out later.
reconciliation.itStaysAsUnappliedCash: It stays on the account as unapplied cash and appears on the reconciliation list. This is the honest answer — guessing it onto an invoice produces one that looks paid and a customer chased for something else.
reconciliation.itIsOnTheAccountAsUnappli: It is on the account as unapplied cash, and on the reconciliation list until somebody works out what it was for.
reconciliation.itHasBeenAppliedToThatInv: It has been applied to that invoice, and the invoice's outstanding figure has come down.
reconciliation.paymentCouldNotBeRecorded: The payment could not be recorded
reconciliation.arrearsCouldNotBeRead: The arrears book could not be read
reconciliation.everyLateInvoiceAndHowFar: Every late invoice, how far it has been chased, and what happens to it next.
reconciliation.decisionsWaiting: {0} waiting on a decision from somebody. Nothing has been done to those customers.
reconciliation.noOpenArrears: No invoice is currently in arrears. Resolved rows are hidden — switch them on to see what has been chased and recovered.
reconciliation.nothingHasEverBeenChased: No invoice has ever been chased on this installation.
reconciliation.andTheDateTheyWereWarnedO: Also the date the customer was warned of in advance.
reconciliation.stageHint.grace: Past its due date and not yet chased. Nothing has been sent to the customer, and invoices routinely pass through here and settle without anyone doing anything.
reconciliation.stageHint.firstNotice: The customer has been told once that the invoice is late. Most accounts stop here.
reconciliation.stageHint.secondNotice: Told a second time. Worth a look at whether the collection is failing for a fixable reason — an expired card will keep failing on its own.
reconciliation.stageHint.finalNotice: The last notice before the account is put in front of somebody. Still nothing but a notice; nothing has been withheld from the customer.
reconciliation.stageHint.restrictionProp: The ladder has run out and this account is waiting on a person to decide what happens. Nothing has been done to the customer and nothing will be done automatically — this platform sits in their authorisation path, so switching them off stops their payments rather than their access to a report. Acting on it is a deliberate change to the organisation's status, made elsewhere.
reconciliation.nothingHasBeenRestricted: Nothing has been restricted. This is a proposal waiting for somebody to decide on, and there is no endpoint on this platform that restricts a customer — acting on it means deliberately changing the organisation's status, which is a different screen. The date below is when the decision was raised, and it is also the date the customer was warned about in advance.
reconciliation.ladderIsNoticesOnly: Every stage on this ladder is a notice. None of them withholds anything from the customer, and nothing here escalates into doing so on its own — the last stage hands the account to a person rather than acting on it.
reconciliation.resolvedRowsAreTheRecover: Resolved rows are how long customers took to pay and how much chasing it took to get there. That is the recovery figure rather than clutter — a board that only shows open arrears can say who is behind, and never whether the chasing works.
reconciliation.waitingOnAPerson: Waiting on a person. Nothing further is scheduled.
reconciliation.neverAttempted: Never collected against. Usually means nothing is on file at the provider to collect from, in which case no number of further attempts will change anything — the customer has to add a method or send a transfer.
reconciliation.currencyDidNotTravel: This row's invoice could not be read beside it, so the amount carries no currency. It is not stated in the platform's own — it is genuinely unknown here, and the invoice itself says which.
reconciliation.allocateEverythingByDefau: Left empty, this applies as much as it can: the smaller of what is on the account and what the invoice still has outstanding. State an amount only to apply less than that.
reconciliation.refundRecordsItOnly: This records the refund on the ledger. It does not send any money: a balance is often made of bank transfers that never went through the payment provider, so there is nothing there to refund against. Somebody still has to make the transfer.
reconciliation.refundReasonIsTheRecord: Printed on the ledger line exactly as typed, and it is the only record of why the money went back. Money handed back without a stated reason is the one entry on a statement nobody can reconstruct afterwards.
revenue.howTheBusinessIsDoing: How the business is doing: what each month's revenue was made of, how much of it rests on how few customers, what serving them cost, and who looks like they are leaving.
revenue.neitherIsInAManagerBundle: Neither of these sits in a Manager's role. Unlike most permissions in this area, they are held only by whoever administers the installation.
revenue.rangeRunsBackwards: The range runs backwards. The first month has to be the earlier one.
revenue.noAnswer.nothingBilled: Nothing was billed in this period, so there is no total to take a proportion of. That is not the same as a share of zero — the question has no answer here.
revenue.noAnswer.noLaddersOpened: No arrears ladder opened in this window, so there was nothing to recover. That is not a recovery rate of zero.
revenue.noAnswer.nothingResolved: Nothing has resolved yet, so there is no time to average. Ordinary for a recent window rather than a fault.
revenue.noAnswer.noBaseline: There is no earlier period to compare against. A new account, not a declining one.
revenue.noAnswer.neverUsed: Never used at all, which is not the same as having last used it a long time ago.
revenue.whatTheMonthWasMadeOf: What each month's revenue was made of: what was won, what grew, what shrank and what left.
revenue.netGrowthIsNotTheHeadline: There is no single growth figure on this screen, and that is deliberate. A book that won fifty and lost forty is a different business from one that won ten and lost nothing, and both grew by ten. The components are the answer.
revenue.movementHint.opening: What the book was worth at the start of the month.
revenue.movementHint.new: Customers billing for the first time. Never merged with reactivation: winning somebody new and winning somebody back are different acts with different costs.
revenue.movementHint.reactivation: Customers who had left and came back. Growth that is mostly this is a retention problem wearing a growth figure's clothes.
revenue.movementHint.expansion: Existing customers billing more than last month.
revenue.movementHint.contraction: Existing customers billing less. Shown even where it cancels expansion exactly, because both still happened.
revenue.movementHint.closing: What the book was worth at the end of the month: opening, plus new, reactivation and expansion, less contraction and churn.
revenue.involuntaryIsInsideChurn: Part of churn, not an addition to it: customers lost because collection failed rather than because they decided to leave. Adding the two counts them twice.
revenue.movesWithinExistingCustomers: This moved within customers already counted in the opening figure, so there is nobody new to count — which is not a count of zero.
revenue.movementDoesNotReconcile: The components do not add up to the stated closing balance — they are out by {0}. The bars above are drawn from the components, so the closing column beside them is not what they reach. Treat both figures with suspicion until this is explained.
revenue.seriesTableCaption: Revenue movement by month across the chosen range.
revenue.movementCouldNotBeRead: The revenue movement could not be read
revenue.noMonthInThisRangeHasBeenBilled: No month in this range has been billed yet. Choose an earlier range, or wait until the first invoice run closes.
revenue.howMuchRestsOnHowFew: How much of a month's revenue rests on how few customers.
revenue.concentrationCouldNotBeRead: The revenue concentration could not be read
revenue.customerCountIsNotATenantCount: Not a count of customers. Anyone whose month net-credited is left out of the total, because a negative contribution would push every share above it past 100%.
revenue.asConcentratedAsEqualCustomers: As concentrated as if all of it came from {0} equally sized customers.
revenue.concentrationIsNotAFault: A reading rather than a verdict. A supplier with four large customers by design is not in trouble — it is in that business.
revenue.monthBilledNothing: No invoice was raised in this month, so there is no total to take shares of. Every figure here would have no denominator — which is not the same as every share being zero.
revenue.concentrationTableCaption: Customers by share of revenue in {0}, largest first.
revenue.whatEachCustomerWasWorth: What each customer was worth that month, against what serving them cost. Worst margin first.
revenue.marginCouldNotBeRead: The margin board could not be read
revenue.costsIncompleteExplained: At least one kind of work this customer used has no cost rate recorded, so it contributed nothing to the cost above. The cost is therefore too low and the margin beside it is too high — not too low. A customer whose usage is entirely uncosted shows a margin of 100%. Record the missing rate under Cost rates.
revenue.someMarginsAreOverstated: {0} row(s) here have incomplete costs, so their margins are overstated rather than understated. They look like the best accounts on the board.
revenue.nobodyHasCostedThis: Nobody has recorded a cost rate for this kind of work, so it adds nothing to the cost. Not a unit cost of zero.
revenue.noCustomerWasBilledThatMonth: No customer was billed in that month, so there is nothing to cost against.
revenue.whetherChasingWorks: Whether chasing late invoices works, and what it costs when it does not.
revenue.recoveryCouldNotBeRead: The recovery figures could not be read
revenue.recoveryIsACohort: These figures cover the arrears ladders that opened in this window, not the ones that closed in it. A window ending recently therefore reports a recovery rate that is still rising, because the ladders it counts have not finished yet. A recent window that looks worse than an older one is usually younger, not worse.
revenue.cohortIsStillMaturing: This window is recent enough that some of its ladders are still running. The rate will rise.
revenue.theCohortItself: The cohort these figures are measured over.
revenue.restrictionsProposedExplained: Ladders that reached the top rung, where a person is asked to decide. Nothing has been done to those customers — this platform has no way to act on its own.
revenue.whereTheLaddersEnded: How far up the ladder each resolved invoice got before it was paid. Every rung is listed, including the ones nothing reached.
revenue.whoLooksLikeTheyAreLeaving: Which customers look like they are drifting away, and the evidence for it. Worst score first.
revenue.healthCouldNotBeRead: The health board could not be read
revenue.scoreIsASortNotAVerdict: The score is a way of ordering this list, not a judgement about a customer. Read the signals beside it — they are the evidence, and the number is only their sum.
revenue.bandHint.healthy: Nothing in this window suggests they are going anywhere.
revenue.bandHint.watch: Something changed that is worth a look before it becomes a conversation.
revenue.bandHint.atRisk: Enough has changed to be worth ringing them about. Still a prompt to go and look, not a finding.
revenue.signalSentence.usageDecline: Usage is down {0} against the previous window.
revenue.signalSentence.usageDeclineUnmea: Usage has fallen, but there is no previous window to measure the fall against.
revenue.signalSentence.errorRateRise: The error rate rose from {0} to {1}.
revenue.signalSentence.silence: Nothing has been sent for {0} days.
revenue.signalSentence.arrears: There is an unpaid invoice being chased.
revenue.signalSentence.noBaseline: There is no earlier traffic to compare this window against. Nothing is wrong — there is simply nothing to measure a change from yet.
revenue.healthTableCaption: Customer health over the last {0} days, worst score first.
revenue.noCustomerHasUsageInThisWindow: No customer has any usage in this window, so there is nothing to compare. Try a longer one.
revenue.recognitionExplained: Revenue recognised per month, as a CSV to carry into a ledger. The same book the panels here are drawn from, in the shape an accountant reconciles against their own.
revenue.recognitionCouldNotBeExported: The recognition export could not be produced
revenue.whatEachKindOfWorkCosts: What each kind of work costs the platform to serve. These are what the margin board measures against.
revenue.ratesCouldNotBeRead: The cost rates could not be read
revenue.ratesAreAppended: Rates are appended, never edited. Last March's margin was worked out against last March's rate, and changing a recorded one would quietly rewrite every month that has already been read. To change a cost, record a new rate.
revenue.resourceHasNoRate: No cost rate has ever been recorded for: {0}. Every customer using that work shows an overstated margin until one is.
revenue.whatItCostsToServeOneUnit: What one unit of this work costs to serve. It applies from the date given, and leaves earlier months measured against the rate they were measured against at the time.
revenue.zeroIsARealRate: Zero is a real rate and is not the same as no rate at all: it says this costs nothing to serve, which completes a margin rather than leaving it overstated.
revenue.leaveEmptyForNow: Leave empty to apply from now. Set a date to record a rate that started applying earlier.
revenue.rateCouldNotBeRecorded: The cost rate could not be recorded
revenue.everyMarginIsOverstatedUntilARat: No cost rate has been recorded at all, so every margin on the board is the customer's full revenue. Record one to make those figures mean something.
